body_markdown:
Replit is a major cloud-based development platform, serving over 60 million users and supporting more than 50 programming languages. However, builders looking for managed infrastructure, different pricing models, or mobile app publishing may find that alternatives such as[Floot](https://floot.com/) better suit their needs.


This guide compares seven Replit alternatives based on features, pricing, backend infrastructure, and deployment capabilities. It also examines how Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) enables app development through supported AI assistants without requiring a separate AI model subscription from Floot.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Full-stack infrastructure simplifies app development** : Floot provides managed infrastructure, including hosting, PostgreSQL databases, authentication, storage, payment integrations, and email services, reducing the need to configure separate backend components.
- **MCP connectors support existing AI workflows** : Floot's MCP connector supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, allowing users to create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, depending on connector permissions.
- **Mobile app publishing is available through Floot** : Floot supports[iOS and Android apps](https://floot.com/en/mobile) from existing web projects. Mobile app builds are available on all Floot plans, with 2 builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. App-store publishing requires developer accounts, while connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan.
- **Action-based pricing separates building from hosting** : Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) provide daily building-action limits of 100 on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power. Hosting is usage-billed beyond included allowances, while optional Floot AI features use separate credits.
- **Code ownership supports long-term flexibility** : Floot users retain ownership of their[code and data](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) across all plans. Database exports are available on every tier, while full project ZIP downloads are included with paid plans.


## **Understanding AI App Development Platforms**


AI app development platforms help founders, business owners, and developers turn natural-language instructions into working applications. Instead of manually writing every component, users describe the functionality they need, while AI systems assist with generating interfaces, backend logic, and application workflows.


An effective app-building platform should support several essential requirements:


- **AI-assisted development** : Generate, edit, and improve applications using natural-language instructions.
- **Backend infrastructure** : Provide databases, authentication, storage, and server-side functionality.
- **Deployment options** : Support web hosting, custom domains, and mobile application workflows.
- **Pricing transparency** : Explain the costs associated with building, hosting, and ongoing application usage.
- **Code ownership** : Clarify whether users can access, export, and migrate their projects.


Replit combines cloud development tools with AI-assisted application building, including its Agent feature. Its effort-based pricing charges according to the computational work performed, meaning simple edits and complex tasks can incur different costs.


Different platforms address these requirements through different approaches, ranging from integrated visual builders to AI agents connected with managed application infrastructure.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that allows users to create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants. It provides managed infrastructure, including hosting, Postgres databases, authentication, storage, and email, while the connected AI assistant handles development.


Instead of requiring users to work exclusively inside a standalone AI builder, Floot connects with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Available building capabilities depend on the connected client's permissions and supported tools. Connector-based development uses the user's existing AI subscription rather than a separate Floot AI build-credit charge.


### **Primary Focus**


- **MCP connector architecture** : Build through supported AI assistants using Floot's[MCP integration](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , with development capabilities determined by connector permissions and client support.
- **Managed backend infrastructure** : Includes Postgres databases, user authentication with Google and Microsoft OAuth, file storage, transactional email, and push notifications.
- **Mobile application development** : Packages web applications into native iOS and Android shells without requiring expertise in Xcode, Android Studio, or React Native.
- **Action-based building limits** : Provides 100 daily building actions on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power. Failed actions do not count against these limits.
- **SEO functionality** : Supports optional server-side pre-rendering, sitemap configuration, robots.txt management, and page metadata settings.


### **How Floot Stands Out**


Floot combines AI-assisted development with managed full-stack infrastructure, helping non-technical founders and business owners create working applications with user accounts, saved data, and deployment capabilities without assembling separate backend services.


- **Managed database and authentication:** Includes[Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) with SQL access, a browser-based table viewer, email-and-password authentication, and Google and Microsoft OAuth.
- **Integrated application services:** Provides CDN-backed file storage, transactional email, push notifications, and background processing. Scheduled and recurring jobs require a paid plan, while certain services need additional configuration.
- **Mobile app publishing:** Supports[iOS and Android](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) builds without requiring Xcode or Android Studio. Floot supports[app store publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) workflows, although developer accounts and final store approval remain necessary. Google Play integration requires a paid Floot plan.
- **Built-in SEO capabilities:** Offers optional server-side pre-rendering, page metadata controls, sitemap configuration, and robots.txt management to support search engine crawlability. Explore the[SEO settings](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) .


### **Organizational Fit & Pricing**


Floot is free to start and offers three primary pricing tiers, with the following monthly subscription prices:


**Free: $0/month**


- 100 building actions per day
- One-time $3 hosting credit at signup
- 2 mobile app builds per month
- Managed application infrastructure
- Web app publishing


**Pro: $25/month**


- 1,000 building actions per day
- 5,000 AI credits per month
- $10 monthly hosting allowance
- 12 mobile app builds per month
- Custom domain support
- Paid project export capabilities


**Power: $100/month**


- 5,000 building actions per day
- 15,000 AI credits per month
- $25 monthly hosting allowance
- Unlimited mobile app builds
- Pro features and higher building allowances


A building action generally represents a metered tool call, such as an edit, read, or test performed by the connected AI assistant. Failed actions are excluded from the count.


Building through the MCP connector uses the connected assistant's own model access. Floot AI credits apply to features such as the optional built-in agent, image generation, and AI functionality inside published applications.


Hosting remains usage-based. Once an included allowance is exhausted, additional usage draws on prepaid hosting credit. Automatic reloading is optional. Users own their project code, application data, and intellectual property across all plans. Database exports are available on every tier, while full project ZIP downloads are included on paid plans for migration or self-hosting.


See the current[Floot pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) and[hosting details](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/hosting) for plan inclusions and usage charges.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable has gained significant traction in AI app development, surpassing $100 million in annual recurring revenue in July 2025, eight months after first reaching $1 million ARR. The platform focuses on generating web applications from natural-language prompts, with integrated AI development, backend services, and visual editing capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Fast prototype generation** : Produces initial working interfaces and applications from natural-language instructions.
- **Backend services** : Lovable Cloud provides database and authentication functionality, with Supabase also available as an integration.
- **Team workspaces** : Supports unlimited workspace members across pricing tiers.
- **Credit-based pricing** : The Free tier provides 5 daily build credits, up to 30 per month, while the standard Pro tier starts with 100 monthly credits.
- **MCP support** : Allows compatible external AI assistants to create, edit, inspect, and deploy Lovable projects.


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable supports development through its integrated AI agent and an MCP connector that enables compatible external assistants to manage projects. The platform also allows published applications to expose integrations that users can access through supported AI assistants.


Credit consumption varies according to the task and development mode. Teams building complex applications should account for repeated iterations, hosting usage, and AI features when estimating costs. For teams exploring a[Lovable alternative](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) , Floot offers integrated native mobile packaging and app-store upload workflows, while Lovable primarily focuses on web application development.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable offers a Free tier with 5 daily build credits, capped at 30 per month. Pro starts at $25/month with 100 monthly credits and rollover options. Business starts at $50/month with 100 monthly credits and additional organizational features.


These are starting prices under monthly billing, with higher credit allocations available through additional pricing tiers. Teams should evaluate expected credit consumption, development frequency, and application hosting requirements.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new focuses on browser-based AI application development, allowing users to move from a natural-language prompt to a working web application without configuring a traditional local development environment. Its workflow emphasizes rapid generation, experimentation, and iteration.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based development** : Provides a development environment accessible through a web browser.
- **Bolt Cloud** : Includes database, authentication, and hosting services.
- **Rapid prototyping** : Supports quick application generation for testing ideas and validating functionality.
- **Mobile development** : Supports mobile application workflows through Expo.


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new uses an integrated AI agent with token-based consumption. The platform supports web applications and mobile development using Expo. Publishing mobile applications to app stores involves additional Expo configuration and store submission steps.


Token consumption can vary based on the size of the project, the complexity of generated code, and the number of development iterations. Teams should consider these factors when estimating the resources required for larger applications.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new offers a Free plan with 1 million tokens per month, subject to a daily limit of 300,000 tokens. Pro starts at $25/month when billed monthly and includes 10 million tokens per month. Teams starts at $30 per member/month under monthly billing.


Organizations should evaluate token consumption, hosting requirements, and expected project complexity before selecting a plan.


## **4. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites allows eligible ChatGPT users to build, preview, publish, and share websites and lightweight web applications directly within ChatGPT. It supports persistent data storage, file uploads, and authentication options for supported use cases.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Conversational building** : Create and refine websites by describing changes in ChatGPT.
- **Hosting and sharing** : Publish websites and manage who can access them.
- **Saved data** : Build workflows that store records, uploaded files, and application state.
- **Authentication** : Supports sign-in and access controls for applicable website workflows.


### **App Building Considerations**


Building and editing ChatGPT Sites counts toward the user's Codex usage, while hosting and storage are governed by separate applicable limits. ChatGPT Sites supports hosted web experiences, including applications that need persistent data and sign-in functionality.


Floot provides a different infrastructure model, with managed Postgres, configurable app-specific authentication, and mobile application packaging for iOS and Android. Floot's MCP-based workflow also supports development through multiple compatible AI assistants rather than depending exclusively on the ChatGPT environment.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available to eligible ChatGPT Plus and Pro users, as well as supported Business and Enterprise workspaces. It is not available on ChatGPT Free or Go plans.


Building and editing count toward Codex usage, while hosting, traffic, and storage are subject to plan-specific allowances and limits. Organizations should consider their existing ChatGPT subscription and application usage requirements when evaluating the service.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 was acquired by Wix in June 2025, bringing the AI application builder into a larger website development ecosystem. The platform provides an AI-led workflow for creating applications through natural-language instructions.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-driven generation** : Converts natural-language descriptions into working applications.
- **Wix ownership** : Base44 became part of Wix following its June 2025 acquisition.
- **Template options** : Provides customizable starting points for common application types.
- **Integrated application services** : Supports application development with backend functionality and deployment features.


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 focuses on simplifying application development through an integrated AI building experience. Its templates can provide starting points for applications such as dashboards, CRMs, scheduling systems, and business tools.


Teams should evaluate the platform's available integrations, credit allowances, and application requirements rather than assuming the Wix acquisition changes specific product capabilities.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 offers a Free plan and multiple paid tiers. Starter costs $20/month with monthly billing or $16/month when billed annually. The plan includes 100 message credits and 2,000 integration credits per month.


Higher tiers provide additional message credits, integration allowances, and features. Organizations should compare their expected development activity and application integration requirements against the available credit allocations.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble combines an established visual application builder with AI-assisted app generation, serving teams that want both conversational development and direct visual control. The platform supports web and native mobile application development with integrated backend capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual workflow builder** : Allows users to design application interfaces and business logic through a graphical environment.
- **AI-assisted generation** : Provides AI-based application generation alongside its visual editor.
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Offers an extensive marketplace of integrations and reusable components.
- **Database and hosting** : Includes infrastructure for developing and deploying applications.
- **Mobile app development** : Supports native mobile application workflows.


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble combines visual programming with AI-assisted development for web and native mobile applications. Users can generate application functionality with AI while retaining direct control over interfaces, workflows, and database structures through the visual editor.


This approach suits teams that prefer explicitly configuring application behavior rather than relying primarily on conversational instructions. The platform's workload-based infrastructure model also means organizations should monitor application usage as traffic and functionality increase.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble offers a Free plan for development, while publishing applications generally requires a paid plan. Its Web & Mobile Starter plan costs $59/month when billed annually or $69/month under monthly billing.


Separate Web and Mobile plans are also available, with different pricing and deployment capabilities. Paid plans include workload allowances, making expected traffic, database activity, and application complexity important considerations.


## **7. v0 by Vercel**


v0 combines AI-powered interface generation with full-stack application development, creating React and Next.js applications from natural-language prompts and images. The platform supports backend functionality and database integrations alongside its frontend generation capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Component generation** : Creates shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS components from natural-language descriptions.
- **Image-to-code functionality** : Converts design references and screenshots into React components.
- **Full-stack support** : Supports backend routes, authentication, and database integrations.
- **Vercel integration** : Provides a deployment workflow connected to Vercel's hosting infrastructure.


### **App Building Considerations**


v0 can generate full-stack applications that include frontend components, backend routes, and authentication functionality. Applications can use services such as Supabase and Neon for persistent data storage.


Some infrastructure capabilities are provisioned through connected services rather than through a single managed application platform. This approach gives teams flexibility in selecting services but may also require evaluating integration configuration, deployment requirements, and associated costs.


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 offers a Free plan, Plus at $30 per user/month, and Business at $100 per user/month. Plus includes $30 in monthly credits per user, with additional daily credits subject to the plan's conditions. Business provides additional organizational and administrative features.


Teams already using Vercel for deployment may find the workflow compatible with their existing infrastructure. Organizations should also account for costs associated with hosting, databases, and other connected services.


## **Why Choose Floot for AI App Building?**


Floot is designed for founders, operators, and businesses that need working full-stack applications without configuring infrastructure separately. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) lets supported AI assistants handle application development while Floot manages hosting, databases, authentication, storage, and deployment.


Users can build applications with saved data, customer accounts, payment integrations, and custom domains. The platform also supports[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android, with app store testing workflows that do not require local mobile development tools. Floot's action-based limits make connector activity easier to monitor. Its hosting allowances and usage-based charges remain separate from the user's existing AI subscription.


Code and data ownership provide flexibility for future development, with database exports available across plans and full project ZIP downloads included on paid tiers. For[non-technical founders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) , Floot offers a practical way to create and maintain applications with managed backend infrastructure.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How does Floot's pricing compare to Replit's effort-based model?**


Floot uses[action-based build tracking](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-actions%20) with daily limits of 100 actions on Free, 1,000 on Pro at $25/month, and 5,000 on Power at $100/month. Metered tool calls include activities such as reading, editing, and testing application files. Failed actions do not count. Replit uses effort-based pricing for its Agent, with checkpoint charges varying according to the computational work performed. Floot separates connector building actions from AI credits and hosting usage.


### **What backend services are included with Floot?**


Floot provides[managed Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , user authentication, file storage, transactional email, push notifications, and application hosting. It supports Google and Microsoft OAuth authentication and integrations with external services such as Stripe for payment processing. Background tasks are available across plans, while scheduled and recurring tasks require a paid plan. Some services require additional configuration, including email-domain verification or external payment credentials.


### **Can Floot be used with Cursor or other code editors?**


Yes. Floot provides a remote MCP server that supports Cursor, VS Code, Zed, and other compatible clients using Streamable HTTP. Developers can work within their preferred code editor while Floot manages backend services, database infrastructure, and deployment. The[editor integration guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/other-mcp-clients) explains how to configure supported clients and authorize access to Floot projects.


### **Does Floot help with SEO for AI-built applications?**


Yes. Floot offers optional server-side pre-rendering so search crawlers can receive page-specific HTML, titles, descriptions, and content. Users can configure sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and individual page metadata through their application settings and AI assistant. The platform provides[SEO configuration](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) and visitor analytics capabilities. Pre-rendering can improve crawlability, although search engine indexing and rankings depend on content quality, technical implementation, and search engine algorithms.


### **What is the MCP connector, and how does it work with Floot?**


The Model Context Protocol is a standard that allows AI assistants to connect with external tools and services. Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) lets users create, edit, test, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development, while Floot provides managed infrastructure. Available capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions and supported tools.
